versions.name: RXV2-0.9.926-posture-follows-map
versions.notes: Before a transmitter is heard, the receiver sets each channel by the flight controller's channel map: roll, pitch, yaw and collective centred, the throttle and every switch low. With the arm switch on channel 5 (for ExpressLRS), channel 5 now starts low.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.925-follows-channel-map
versions.notes: The receiver and the phone's Switches, Rescue and Transmitter channels pages now follow Rotorflight's channel map. With the arm switch moved to channel 5 (for ExpressLRS), the receiver watches the right channel for arming, and the pages name the right channel.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.924-sim-restart-quiet
versions.notes: In simulator mode a receiver that restarts with the transmitter off now goes straight to the saved failsafe positions (motor off). Before, it gave the simulator its start-up positions, which on some simulator models meant motor ON. With no failsafe saved, the motor channel chosen for the spool-up is held off until a transmitter is heard. Real models are unchanged: at power-up they are never given the saved positions.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.923-fc-says-armed
versions.notes: The app no longer says ARMED, or refuses the Rotorflight pages, while the flight controller says the model is not armed (an arm switch that is on but refused, or on another channel than the transmitter's model uses). With a flight controller answering, the pages and the red banner go by its own word. Arming still locks the pages at once. Restarting or updating the receiver and saving the failsafe still need the arm switch off.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.922-hold-3s
versions.notes: A gap in the radio link of under 3 seconds now changes nothing: the receiver holds the last positions for 3 seconds (it was 1.5) before failsafe, and the transmitter (B208) waits the same 3 seconds before it calls the model lost. Update the transmitter too.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.921-app-lets-go
versions.notes: A phone app left in the background no longer keeps the transmitter from connecting by Bluetooth: when the transmitter's Rotorflight pages ask, the receiver lets a silent app go within seconds (it kept it for 10 minutes before). An app in use keeps its link.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.920-review
versions.notes: Safety: the transmitter's Save failsafe is refused while the model is armed, as the app's own Save already was. On a dongle the pages say dongle again, and the factory-reset page names the address the board comes back on (Untitled.local). From the code review of 10 Nov 2026.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.919-fc-line-auto-on
versions.notes: 0.9.919: the 'a flight controller is on this line' switch turns itself on when Rotorflight answers (on the line or over USB) or was seen here before; unticking it on purpose forgets the flight controller, so the receiver never fights the pilot. A plain servo converter never answers MSP, so it is never mistaken for one.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.918-fc-line-switch
versions.notes: 0.9.918: the Protocol page's 'a flight controller is on this line' switch explained; unticking it with a Rotorflight FC present asks first; the home page warns when it is off and switches it back on with one button (BT1 had it off: no volts or RPM, the collective held low at power-up).

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.917-fc-armed-word
versions.notes: With a Rotorflight flight controller answering, its own word on ARMED now rules the radios: Bluetooth and WiFi stay up while it says disarmed, transmitter on or off, and go down when it says armed. The arming channel is only a fallback. The Receiver settings page says when the saved failsafe applies.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.916-servo-copy-honest
versions.notes: The Servos page's 'Copy to servos 2 & 3' now says plainly when a write did not happen; it said Copied whatever became of the writes. The receiver takes one Bluetooth connection at a time: with the transmitter on a Rotorflight page the app cannot write, and the other way round.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.915-read-back-window
versions.notes: A block just written to the flight controller keeps streaming to the transmitter for 3 s after the save is confirmed, so the transmitter's read-back sees the new values even when its own request was lost (with transmitter B177).

rotorflight.line: Rotorflight 2.3 — the release these pages are written and tested against.
